conventions.convention: The cross product is right-handed; [ω]×z=ω×z. Rotation covariance requires R∈SO(3), including det R=1.

A mass distribution is a positive-total-mass finite Borel measure concentrated, up to a measurable null set, in some closed ball of positive radius. Completeness, a density, and absence of atoms are not assumed. Centred means ∫ρ dν=0.
Moment finiteness invokes ACω through the cited continuity-to-Borel-measurability supplier; integrals of vectors and matrices are componentwise scalar Lebesgue integrals.

Rigid placement is x(t,ρ)=c(t)+R(t)ρ on a nondegenerate time interval. Body angular velocity satisfies RᵀR′=[ω]×; spatial angular velocity is Rω. Differentiability is componentwise and domain-relative, including included endpoints.
Principal-coordinate cross-product component equations use a positively oriented orthonormal eigenbasis. The torque balance (Rl)′=τ is an explicit mathematical hypothesis, not a derived physical law.

Nonlinear spin theorems assume 0<I₁<I₂<I₃ and L≠0. The linearized theorem instead permits arbitrary pairwise distinct positive diagonal entries and Ω≠0; it does not require realization by a mass distribution.

Euler angles use Θ(φ,θ,ψ)=Rz(φ)Ry(θ)Rz(ψ), with φ,ψ real and 0<θ<π. No injectivity or chart property is assumed. The heavy-top system is defined by its three displayed differential equations, with positive parameters and potential term +mgd cos θ in the energy.

load_bearing.statement: The map ω↦[ω]× is a linear bijection from R³ onto the skew-symmetric matrices, satisfies [ω]×z=ω×z, and satisfies R[ω]×Rᵀ=[Rω]× for every R∈SO(3).

Under ACω, a finite bounded Borel measure on R³ has integrable coordinate and coordinate-product functions; its first moment and inertia entries are finite, with the stated Rν(R³) and 2R²ν(R³) bounds.

Under ACω, I is symmetric and ωᵀIω=∫‖ω×ρ‖² dν≥0. For ω≠0 this vanishes exactly when ν(R³\Rω)=0. Thus I is positive definite exactly when every origin line has positive mass off it, and then I is invertible.
For entrywise differentiable matrix curves, differentiation respects sums and transpose and satisfies (AB)′=A′B+AB′. For an SO(3)-valued curve, AᵀA′ and A′Aᵀ are skew-symmetric and have trace zero.
Under ACω, for a centred mass distribution and differentiable rigid placement, the defining energy and relative angular-momentum integrands are integrable, K=½m‖c′‖²+½ωᵀIω, and Lc=RIω.

Under the stated centred nondegenerate mass-distribution and regularity hypotheses and balance (Rl)′=τ, Iω′+ω×Iω=Rᵀτ. If τ=0, l′=l×I⁻¹l and ‖l‖² and ½⟨l,I⁻¹l⟩ are constant; the displayed component equations hold in a positively oriented principal basis.
Θ maps R×(0,π)×R to SO(3) by Rz(φ)Ry(θ)Rz(ψ). For positive A,C,m,d,g, heavy-top trajectories are twice-differentiable curves in this domain satisfying the three displayed equations.
Every heavy-top trajectory has constant b=C(ψ′+φ′cos θ) and a=Aφ′sin²θ+b cos θ, the displayed reconstructed rates, constant reduced energy E=½Aθ′²+U(θ), and Aθ″=−U′(θ).

concerns.concern: Proof step 2.2, items/thm-cm-heavy-top-reduction.md:87, gives the intermediate equality φ′(Aφ′sin²θ+C cosθ(ψ′+φ′cosθ))+ψ′C(ψ′+φ′cosθ)−½C(ψ′+φ′cosθ)²=½C(ψ′+φ′cosθ)². Its left side actually equals Aφ′²sin²θ+½C(ψ′+φ′cosθ)². For θ=π/2, φ′=1, ψ′=0 it equals A while the stated right side is zero. The final energy formula is correct, and direct expansion closes the proof immediately, but this displayed intermediate computation is false.

alerts.finding: Page library/non-relativistic-quantum-mechanics-mathematics/qm-math-orbital-and-spin.md:62–65 describes the displayed Jz and J± matrices as 'self-adjoint'. The cited prop-nrqm-orbital-and-spin-finite-spin-matrices, Statement (a), correctly asserts self-adjointness of Jz,Jx,Jy and J+*=J−. For s=1/2, J+ has matrix [[0,1],[0,0]], which is not self-adjoint. This is a false page-summary assertion; the supplying proposition is correct.

seams_checked.note: The nonlinear spin proofs use the autonomous compact-state trapping clause of cor-cm-finite-time-breakdown-requires-escape after checking continuity and local Lipschitzness; invariant spheres supply compact subsets of U=R³.
SO(3), its inverse and group properties, and the maximal-solution Lyapunov-stability definition are used with their stated domains and conventions.
pthm-cm03-frame-transformations L3 derives cross-product covariance from clauses 1 and 3 of the skew correspondence for R∈SO(3).
The moving-frame definition and inertial-force theorem preserve the body convention RᵀR′ and convert to spatial angular velocity by Rω using the conjugation law.

Consumers retain positive finite bounded mass, centering, ACω for integrals, and sufficient C² regularity. The orientation remark proves its additional local-chart claim using the angular-velocity differential and a manifold inverse-function theorem rather than attributing it to the parametrization definition.

Atomic inertia computations preserve centering and degeneracy qualifications. The pole example explicitly extends the displayed rotation formula to R³ rather than treating excluded θ=0 as belonging to the supplier's domain.

Euler and invariant consumers retain the torque-balance and nondegeneracy premises. Linearized and nonlinear stability claims are separated; principal-coordinate orientation and heavy-top θ∈(0,π) restrictions are preserved.
The steady-precession example uses the same RzRyRz angular-velocity formula and heavy-top reduction, with pivot moments A=3,C=1 and declared dimensionless time convention.
The shifted-inertia definition explicitly distinguishes the zero measure from positive-mass distributions. The parallel-axis theorem retains centering, positive total mass and ACω.
The two-point parallel-axis example has positive weights, bounded support and vanishing first moment, and keeps ACω for the integrals.

The orbital-generator item's finite rotation identities use the same right-handed skew/cross correspondence and SO(3) conjugation conventions. The separate page-summary self-adjointness error is routed in alerts.
